- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope or add a ceiling to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 80+), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to reflect earlier trend reversal.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in early 30d horizon — add 2–3% buffer to forecast for high volatility periods.  
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model often overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging true trend — apply a 1–2 day lead-in adjustment if sentiment is trending upward.
